scope: The 55 previously high-confidence unsuitable/literal rows kept open by the 592-hold policy because source-specific questions remained.
method: Read exact source sentence, prior per-row reason and current hold decision. Resolved the specific source/owner/target question without repeating assessments. Primary Cambridge lexical evidence is linked where conventionality or sense could change the verdict. Natural collocations were not rejected solely for lacking fixed-idiom status; distinct course-level decisions remain necessary.

rows.expression: keep life running smoothly
rows.exactSourceSentence: A calendar helps keep life running smoothly.
rows.reason: The calendar sentence uses the transparent causative keep X running smoothly; owner1353 requires the oil image, absent here. No bounded idiomatic unit survives without adding wording.
rows.nextGate: Document non-course; do not stretch owner1353.

rows.expression: pull on a thread and unravel a whole family story
rows.exactSourceSentence: One old photograph can pull on a thread and unravel a whole family story.
rows.reason: Pull on a thread may be reusable discovery imagery, but the source joins it to unravel a whole family story. Isolating the first clause could change the taught cause/result decision.
rows.nextGate: Check primary usage and pilot a bounded lemma before any rejection or lesson.

rows.expression: connected to home
rows.exactSourceSentence: A phone helps children feel connected to home.
rows.reason: A phone enabling children to feel connected to home has its ordinary communication meaning; the figurative connection is supplied by context and adds no distinct decision.

rows.expression: enjoying the fruit while ignoring the labour that grew it
rows.exactSourceSentence: Piracy is like enjoying the fruit while ignoring the labour that grew it.
rows.reason: The piracy comparison is a complete bespoke harvest analogy; fruit, labour and piracy must stay together to convey its moral point.

rows.expression: dominate the scroll
rows.exactSourceSentence: Short videos can dominate the scroll for weeks.
rows.reason: Dominate the scroll is understandable but may be a transferable digital-attention collocation rather than a single-source image; prior report has not established productive usage or a bounded detector.
rows.nextGate: Check primary corpus/usage and seven-step transferability; otherwise document non-course.

rows.expression: a key turning in an old door
rows.exactSourceSentence: The melody felt like a key turning in an old door.
rows.reason: The melody/key/old-door construction is a one-off memory simile; no stable target can be isolated without losing the trigger-memory link.

rows.expression: passed hand to hand, heart to heart
rows.exactSourceSentence: The story was passed hand to hand, heart to heart.
rows.reason: The paired hand-to-hand/heart-to-heart rhyme expresses personal circulation. Dictionary heart-to-heart means an honest private conversation, a different sense; taking that conventional unit would misteach the source.
rows.nextGate: Document creative parallelism, not an alias to heart-to-heart.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary noun/adjective means a candid personal conversation, not the source’s personal transmission of a story.

rows.expression: news has moved from being a destination to being part of the feed
rows.exactSourceSentence: For many users, news has moved from being a destination to being part of the feed.
rows.reason: The full destination-versus-feed statement is a topical essay contrast, not a separable lexical unit; teaching destination alone would miss incidental news exposure.

rows.expression: minor setbacks
rows.exactSourceSentence: Minor setbacks can help learners practise patience.
rows.reason: Minor setbacks is compositional adjective+noun for small difficulties. A broader ordinary-setbacks owner would add the modifier but no new learner decision.
rows.nextGate: Document transparent collocation; do not broaden owner solely for coverage.

rows.expression: love is the foundation
rows.exactSourceSentence: In our family, love is the foundation of every rule.
rows.reason: Love is the foundation of every rule is a productive X-is-the-foundation-of-Y metaphor; parenting context supplies the meaning. Existing foundation lessons do not need this as a separate owner.

rows.expression: the sweet stops being just food
rows.exactSourceSentence: When every success earns candy, the sweet stops being just food.
rows.reason: The sweet stops being just food is a one-sentence contrast about candy as reward; neither stop being just nor the full candy claim is a stable target here.

rows.expression: a kind of trophy
rows.exactSourceSentence: The snack became a kind of trophy rather than an occasional treat.
rows.reason: A snack as a kind of trophy is an explicitly signalled comparison; the status/reward inference requires the candy context, not a reusable trophy construction.

rows.expression: fix the roof before hanging the flags
rows.exactSourceSentence: The council should fix the roof before hanging the flags.
rows.reason: Fix the roof before hanging the flags is a bespoke priority analogy for council spending. A literal roof reading and policy reading cannot be separated by a narrow reusable unit.

rows.expression: solo decisions often feel lighter
rows.exactSourceSentence: For lunch plans, solo decisions often feel lighter.
rows.reason: Solo decisions feeling lighter uses productive burden imagery; lunch plans explain why the decision feels easier, but the phrase has no fixed lexical boundary.

rows.expression: that spark
rows.exactSourceSentence: One surprising question provided that spark.
rows.reason: That spark is an anaphoric noun whose referent is the preceding surprising question. A lesson would have to invent the missing antecedent or teach generic spark instead.

rows.expression: think beyond what is directly in front of them
rows.exactSourceSentence: Stories help children think beyond what is directly in front of them.
rows.reason: Think beyond what is directly in front of them is ordinary spatial extension to imagination; it is a freely assembled clause, not a bounded expression.

rows.expression: not endlessly so
rows.exactSourceSentence: I can be patient, but not endlessly so.
rows.reason: Not endlessly so is ordinary so-anaphora qualifying patient; it is a grammar example rather than a distinct expression from this source.

rows.expression: patience can be nurtured
rows.exactSourceSentence: With practice, patience can be nurtured.
rows.reason: Patience can be nurtured extends the ordinary develop/care sense of nurture; the plant image has no independent target boundary here.

rows.expression: life has a way of bringing old words back with new meaning
rows.exactSourceSentence: Years later, he discovered that life has a way of bringing old words back with new meaning.
rows.reason: Life bringing old words back with new meaning is a full reflective personification; stripping away its context leaves no single reusable phrase.

rows.expression: pay attention to nuance
rows.exactSourceSentence: Writers should pay attention to nuance in word choice.
rows.reason: Pay attention to nuance is natural instructional prose, but the source simply asks writers to notice meaning/tone differences. It adds no seven-decision boundary beyond the existing verb phrase.
rows.nextGate: Document ordinary instructional collocation; P79 naturalness alone does not require a lesson.

rows.expression: vague intentions into clearer action
rows.exactSourceSentence: A written plan can turn vague intentions into clearer action.
rows.reason: The proposed span omits the governing turn in the exact sentence. The full turn vague intentions into clearer action is freely compositional planning prose.

rows.expression: life does not always move in a straight line
rows.exactSourceSentence: Her career shows that life does not always move in a straight line.
rows.reason: Selected owner4548 teaches progress is not a straight line, the same nonlinear-career inference. Source3352 is earlier, so direct alias to 4548 conflicts with earliest-source ownership; this is an ownership migration, not a non-course item.
rows.nextGate: Adjudicate earliest-source owner/provenance migration and preserve selected lesson history.

rows.expression: gadget-heavy
rows.exactSourceSentence: Their new office is gadget-heavy but easy to use.
rows.reason: Gadget-heavy transparently uses productive X-heavy morphology to mean containing many gadgets. The office contrast supplies the only nuance; no distinct seven-step target is demonstrated.
rows.nextGate: Document productive compound; reconsider only for a general X-heavy morphology lesson.

rows.expression: a stamp of reassurance
rows.exactSourceSentence: The warranty felt like a stamp of reassurance.
rows.reason: Stamp of reassurance is a one-off warranty-as-seal image; source does not supply a reusable stamp-of-X construction.

rows.expression: the story, image, or lifestyle wrapped around it
rows.exactSourceSentence: Buyers sometimes want the story, image, or lifestyle wrapped around it.
rows.reason: Story, image, or lifestyle wrapped around a product is a long contextual fragment, not a stable wrapping idiom. The buyer association must be inferred from the whole sentence.

rows.expression: judgment still has to be built the slow way
rows.exactSourceSentence: Facts are quick to find, but judgment still has to be built the slow way.
rows.reason: Judgment built the slow way is an aphoristic counterpoint to quick facts. Built and slow way are productive words, not a source-supported target unit.

rows.expression: a promise before the box is even opened
rows.exactSourceSentence: The familiar logo feels like a promise before the box is even opened.
rows.reason: The logo as a promise before opening the box is a brand-expectation image tied to packaging; no stable promise-before-X expression is supported.

rows.expression: tackles both the symptoms and the roots of the problem
rows.exactSourceSentence: A good policy tackles both the symptoms and the roots of the problem.
rows.reason: Earlier source-specific adjudication found symptoms and roots are two independent productive metaphors. Replacing roots with root causes to make an idiom would rewrite the exact source.
rows.nextGate: Document mixed-metaphor clause; retain original wording as provenance.

rows.expression: a locked door
rows.exactSourceSentence: Before the class, chemistry felt like a locked door.
rows.reason: Chemistry felt like a locked door is grammatical, understandable barrier imagery, but the subject+simile is productive and not a fixed locked-door unit. The source supplies no narrower advanced contrast.
rows.nextGate: Document source-specific simile; no normalization needed.

rows.expression: focused blocks
rows.exactSourceSentence: She revises in focused blocks of twenty minutes.
rows.reason: Focused blocks of twenty minutes plainly denotes timed study sessions; block length and focus are literal schedule details, with no distinct meaning shift.

rows.expression: real life does not come with an instruction manual
rows.exactSourceSentence: Real life does not come with an instruction manual for every crisis.
rows.reason: Real life does not come with an instruction manual is a complete aphorism; the crisis qualifier makes the practical-judgment point. It does not isolate a smaller target without replacing the source.

rows.expression: add noise with one hand and take it away with the other
rows.exactSourceSentence: New transport can add noise with one hand and take it away with the other.
rows.reason: Owner3431 teaches giving a benefit while taking it away. This source says transport adds noise in one place and takes it away in another; changed verb and mixed effects are close but not automatically the same lesson or detectable pattern.
rows.nextGate: Review idiomatic acceptability and same-sense owner3431 scope; no automatic alias.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary indexes fixed hand expressions; source changes the give/take paired construction and requires owner comparison.

rows.expression: repair small cracks
rows.exactSourceSentence: A kind word can repair small cracks between friends.
rows.reason: A kind word repairing cracks between friends is productive relationship-as-building imagery. No fixed repair-cracks-between-X unit or separate learner choice is evident.

rows.expression: pieces of heritage made tangible
rows.exactSourceSentence: These garments are pieces of heritage made tangible.
rows.reason: Garments called pieces of heritage made tangible is poetic description of tangible culture; made tangible is compositional and the heritage subject is topic-bound.

rows.expression: carry the fingerprints of a culture
rows.exactSourceSentence: Local ceramics carry the fingerprints of a culture.
rows.reason: Ceramics carrying a culture’s fingerprints extends unique-mark imagery. Dictionary fingerprints are all over something is a different responsibility/trace idiom; normalizing to it would change source sense.
rows.nextGate: Document bespoke cultural-mark image; avoid idiom alias.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary lists fingerprints are all over something as an idiom; source cultural-mark image is not that construction.

rows.expression: learned a new accent
rows.exactSourceSentence: The imported celebration seemed to have learned a new accent.
rows.reason: An imported celebration learning a new accent is deliberate personification of cultural adaptation; the literal accent target belongs to speech, not events.

rows.expression: made with a bit more soul
rows.exactSourceSentence: The handmade chair felt made with a bit more soul.
rows.reason: Made with a bit more soul is subjective but may be a natural reusable evaluation of handmade work. The exact transferable target and contrast with mere quality are not established.
rows.nextGate: Check primary usage/register and pilot distinct decisions before accepting or closing.

rows.expression: locked in a glass box
rows.exactSourceSentence: A living culture should not be locked in a glass box.
rows.reason: A living culture locked in a glass box is an invented display-case image; the living-versus-preserved contrast depends on the full sentence.

rows.expression: spend a few hours in the air
rows.exactSourceSentence: They would rather spend a few hours in the air than take a ferry.
rows.reason: Spend a few hours in the air denotes ordinary plane travel in direct contrast with a ferry; no figurative or advanced usage decision is present.

rows.expression: getting from one place to another
rows.exactSourceSentence: The app makes getting from one place to another easier.
rows.reason: Getting from one place to another plainly means travel between locations. The app context adds convenience but no lexical contrast.

rows.expression: dropping a stone into still water
rows.exactSourceSentence: The new policy was like dropping a stone into still water.
rows.reason: The policy was like dropping a stone into still water is an explicitly marked one-off simile. The source does not say ripple, so expanding an earlier ripple detector would substitute the inferred effect for the words used.
rows.nextGate: Document source simile; do not create ripple alias from inference.

rows.expression: clear the roads
rows.exactSourceSentence: Better buses may help clear the roads.
rows.reason: Better buses clearing roads directly means reducing vehicles/congestion on roads; the physical traffic meaning is intended, with no separate metaphor.

rows.expression: a huge chunk of their break
rows.exactSourceSentence: The coach ride used a huge chunk of their break.
rows.reason: A huge chunk of their break is transparent informal large-portion wording; coach travel provides the quantity, not a special idiom.

rows.expression: the choice starts to make itself
rows.exactSourceSentence: With only two days off, the choice starts to make itself.
rows.reason: The choice starts to make itself personifies an easy decision; this may be a reusable decision-becomes-obvious formula, but the current source alone does not establish conventionality or a bounded variant.
rows.nextGate: Check primary usage and a seven-step decision boundary before closure.

rows.expression: work within tight budgets
rows.exactSourceSentence: Councils must work within tight budgets.
rows.reason: Councils working within tight budgets plainly means operating with limited funds. This is natural administrative collocation, but no nonliteral or distinct course-level contrast is shown.
rows.nextGate: Document ordinary budget constraint; P79 requires more than naturalness.

rows.expression: repair the roof while still living in the house
rows.exactSourceSentence: Transit planners must repair the roof while still living in the house.
rows.reason: Repair the roof while living in the house is a bespoke analogy for improving transit while service continues. Exact image and active-system inference depend on the whole sentence.

rows.expression: the real battle
rows.exactSourceSentence: For the project, the real battle was public trust.
rows.reason: The real battle was public trust uses broad conflict-as-difficulty language; the clause gives its own referent and no fixed target beyond battle.

rows.expression: the noise of ordinary life has been turned right down
rows.exactSourceSentence: On holiday, the noise of ordinary life has been turned right down.
rows.reason: Noise of ordinary life turned right down is a bespoke volume-control image for holiday relief. No stable segment carries the full meaning independently.

rows.expression: open eyes and an open mind
rows.exactSourceSentence: She explored the city with open eyes and an open mind.
rows.reason: Open eyes and an open mind pairs attentive observation with receptive judgment. Owner423 has go in with an open mind, but its construction and single mental-state decision differ; a bounded alias needs scope review.
rows.nextGate: Compare source to owner423 and test whether paired phrase warrants its own unit; do not collapse both halves.

rows.expression: keeps businesses alive
rows.exactSourceSentence: Weekend tourism keeps businesses alive.
rows.reason: Keep businesses alive expresses economic survival; existing keep-history/relationships/curiosity-alive owners have different referents and decisions. P79 permits natural reusable collocations, so mere transparency cannot settle this.
rows.nextGate: Test a bounded business-continuity lesson versus a documented ordinary-use exclusion.

rows.expression: an outsider's eyes
rows.exactSourceSentence: Sometimes an outsider's eyes reveal local beauty.
rows.reason: Outsider’s eyes is a productive fresh-viewpoint metaphor, but the source’s possessive and plural eyes need target-form review. Existing fresh-eyes lessons may be related without exact owner equivalence.
rows.nextGate: Compare viewpoint owner(s) and natural grammar before disposition.

rows.expression: not infinitely absorbent
rows.exactSourceSentence: A small beach is not infinitely absorbent.
rows.reason: Not infinitely absorbent applies a material-capacity image to a beach. The unusual adjective requires the visitor-capacity context and provides no stable unit.

rows.expression: a real boost to the economy
rows.exactSourceSentence: Tourism can be a real boost to the economy.
rows.reason: Cambridge records noun boost to the economy as an ordinary but natural collocation; P79 allows collocations. The unresolved question is whether real boost adds a distinct advanced learner decision, not whether the wording exists.
rows.nextGate: Run course-value/seven-decision gate; if thin, document non-course with this dictionary evidence.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary noun examples include boost to the economy, confirming the ordinary natural collocation.

rows.expression: postcard image may catch the eye
rows.exactSourceSentence: A postcard image may catch the eye, but service earns a return visit.
rows.reason: Catch the eye is a conventional attention idiom; owner3495 teaches catch someone’s eye but its detector requires a possessive and rejects source catch the eye. The postcard image is contextual and should not be the target.
rows.nextGate: Review bounded the-eye variant and visual-attention owner3495 before disposition.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary lists catch someone’s eye as attracting visual attention, matching source sense but leaving the-eye form to owner review.

rows.expression: a restful hotel is golden
rows.exactSourceSentence: After a long flight, a restful hotel is golden.
rows.reason: Cambridge gives golden a special/advantageous sense, so the hotel praise is natural rather than invented. Whether predicative X is golden yields seven distinct advanced decisions remains unresolved.
rows.nextGate: Check predicative register and course value; do not equate with golden ticket or opportunity.

primaryLexicalEvidence.evidence: Dictionary adjective includes special/successful/advantageous, confirming a nonliteral praise sense.

limits: These are proposals, not decision edits or editorial acceptance. Owner migration, bounded aliases and seven-step feasibility remain open for the keep-open rows. No audio, release or live claim.
